record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Polyomino Tilings
record.original_question: Does there exist a connected polyomino that admits tilings of the plane, but every such tiling is non-periodic? In other words, is there an aperiodic polyomino?

evidence.quote: Non-isohedral tilings may be partitioned into two types: periodic tilings with (some) symmetries, and non-periodic tilings with no symmetries.
No connected shapes that have only non-periodic tilings, called aperiodic shapes, are known
Open Problem 5 Is there an aperiodic polyomino?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polyomino is a connected planar shape formed by gluing finitely many unit squares of the integer lattice edge-to-edge. A tiling of the plane by congruent copies of a polyomino P is a covering of the plane by translates, rotations, and reflections of P with pairwise disjoint interiors. Such a tiling is periodic if it is invariant under translation by two linearly independent vectors, and non-periodic otherwise. A polyomino P is called aperiodic if P admits at least one tiling of the plane and every tiling of the plane by congruent copies of P is non-periodic.

Question: Does there exist an aperiodic polyomino?
artifact.status_search_result: Although the einstein problem for general planar tiles was resolved in 2023 by Smith, Myers, Kaplan, and Goodman-Strauss with the "hat" aperiodic monotile, the hat is a polykite and not a polyomino. Exhaustive searches reported on polyomino tiling resources have not found any aperiodic polyomino, and the question of whether an aperiodic polyomino exists is still listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Polyform tiling
status_evidence.snippet: Within the ranges covered by these tables, there are no aperiodic polyominoes, polyhexes or polyiamonds, and two aperiodic polykites.
status_evidence.claim: No aperiodic polyomino is known among exhaustively searched polyominoes.

status_evidence.title: Aperiodic Monotile -- from Wolfram MathWorld
status_evidence.snippet: Smith et al. (2023) found a simple polykite known as a hat that is an aperiodic monotile.
status_evidence.claim: The aperiodic monotile found in 2023 is a polykite, not a polyomino, so the polyomino version remains separate.
